Subject: Preliminary incident snapshot for QBR prep — request for concise owner reads

Team and OrbitAI partners,

As we pull together QBR material next week I need a tight, single-slide summary of the recent multi-region inference degradation on Apr 6-7 that impacted OrbitAI and a few other enterprise customers. The board will ask three things: what happened, what we did, and how we will prevent recurrence (quantifiable).

Ask: can each owner provide a 2–4 bullet summary plus a single line for ongoing risk and an owner for that risk? Please include a one-line SLA impact (e.g., "p50 increase +80ms for 18h; three customers >SLA"). I want entries aligned to the action register we keep in the Drive.

Attached is my rough postmortem draft and a heatmap dump from the incident window — please update and return by EOD Tue so I can fold into the QBR pack. We will keep external language clear — Lindsey/Taurean, expect a customer-facing one-pager after we lock owners.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf, sla-heatmap-202704.csv

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher

Subject: Re: Preliminary incident snapshot for QBR prep — request for concise owner reads

Sean — sending technical owner read; keeping to the 4-line limit.

What happened:
- Rapid KV-cache churn during a model swap caused suboptimal batching; kernel fallback triggered higher tail latency around 03:18–05:40 UTC on 6 Apr.

What we did:
- Emergency rollback to last-stable model variant at 04:02 UTC; mitigated error amplification by throttling cold-start traffic with a short-lived quota.

Ongoing risk & owner:
- Risk: model-variant compatibility matrix not fully validated for nonstandard seq-len distributions. Owner: Hannah Schmitt (Reliability).

SLA impact (conservative): p50 +82ms, p95 +420ms across two regions; three customers experienced SLA violations (OrbitAI included).

Notes: I updated section 2 of the postmortem (attached) with kernel traces and a proposed test checklist for model onboarding. I flagged a medium-priority test gap: automated kernel-selection smoke tests for quantized variants.

[Attachment: postmortem-draft.pdf (updated)]

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

Redwood Inference

Adding ops / customer action items from my side — keeping for the action register.

Immediate remediations completed:
- Implemented temporary routing rule (region fallback) to reduce blast radius — rolled 2027-04-06 06:10 UTC.
- Increased autoscaler headroom for affected pools; short-term cap raised by 12% to avoid queuing.

Follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- Action: Expand model-variant smoke-test coverage. Owner: Hannah. ETA: 2027-05-10.
- Action: Formalize escalation ladder for cross-region SLA breaches (who pages who). Owner: Marissa Cole. ETA: 2027-04-30.
- Action: Customer remediation package (credits + postmortem one-pager). Owner: Sean Gallagher. ETA: 2027-04-24.

I pushed an updated action-register (action-register-april.xlsx) to the Drive and linked items to HS-Record-3921 for tracking. I'm marking the escalation-ladder doc as DRAFT; please review and suggest pager names if you think others need to be included.

Quick infra note for the QBR slide (technical appendix):
- Root cause refinement: A rare combination of sequencing distribution and an aggressive kernel selection heuristic caused a deterministic latency cliff for quantized-run paths. Not a hardware failure.
- Mitigation plan: Conservative kernel-selection threshold for upcoming releases + deploy a canary variant with extended seq-len coverage. Owner: Connor O'Brien (Infrastructure). ETA: 2027-05-07.

Also: I recommend we include a one-line SLA mitigation metric we can promise on the QBR: "By EOW May, we will reduce model-variant incompatibility risk score by 60% (measured by canary failures per 1000 requests)."

-C
Connor O'Brien
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
